Yemen Financial Inclusion Evidence

Financial inclusion in Yemen is not one number.

Yemen Financial Inclusion Evidence is a bilingual public resource on financial inclusion in Yemen. For each figure, it shows what the evidence establishes and what it does not, when and for whom the figure applies, and where it comes from.

Start with a questionVerify evidence
Evidence

Three figures, three different things measured

11.9% of adults aged 15 and over in the areas surveyed had an account at a financial institution or with a mobile-money provider, according to the latest representative population measure: the World Bank’s Global Findex 2021 survey of Yemen (fieldwork 7 November 2022 to 9 January 2023; World Bank data year 2022). Areas holding about 23% of the population were not surveyed.

When was it measured or observed?World Bank reporting year 2022; Global Findex 2021 study; Yemen fieldwork 2022-11-07 to 2023-01-09
Account ownership: the representative measure from the Global Findex 2021 wave
Adults 15+ in survey coverage
Open evidence record

In the same survey, 18.35% of men and 5.44% of women had an account, a gap of 12.91 percentage points.

When was it measured or observed?2021 Findex wave (survey round); Yemen fieldwork 2022-11-07 to 2023-01-09
A measured gender gap in account ownership
Adults 15+ in survey coverage
Open evidence record

Separately, point-of-sale (POS) terminals reported by the Central Bank of Yemen – Aden (CBY-Aden) rose from 561 in March 2025 to 1,651 in June 2026, within CBY-Aden’s reporting scope.

When was it measured or observed?Mar-2025–Jun-2026
POS infrastructure expanded
POS terminals within the payment-system reporting scope of the Central Bank of Yemen – Aden (CBY-Aden); how far that scope covers each area of Yemen is not established.
Open evidence record

These are different measures: people, a disparity within one survey, and infrastructure. None substitutes for another.

What this does not establish

What should not be inferred?

More infrastructure does not by itself prove that more people are using financial services. A licensed institution is not proof that every listed location is operating. Access does not prove use; use does not prove service quality or impact; and the number of accounts is not the number of people.

Common starting questions

Questions to start from

Start from the problem you need to resolve. Choose the question closest to the decision or uncertainty in front of you. Each question leads to its answer, the answer’s limits and the way to verify it.

  1. Who is being left behind — and where are the measured gaps?
    Population measures, disparities within the same wave (survey round) and what the evidence cannot explain.
  2. Are reforms and payment infrastructure turning into access, use, quality and outcomes?
    A stage-by-stage chain from rule to result.
  3. For firms, how serious a constraint is finance — and how does it compare with other constraints?
    How often finance is named among other constraints, how severe the finance obstacle is for a defined group of firms, the credit path and programme evidence.
  4. How can I check the evidence behind a claim, see why sources disagree and reproduce a result?
    Evidence records, field-by-field comparison, how derived figures are calculated, and how to cite them.

Analysis

Different evidence describes different moments.

Population surveys, administrative payment data, provider-status decisions, programme reports and macroeconomic series are updated on different schedules. Each conclusion therefore carries the period it actually covers. “Latest” means latest for that question or measure, not latest for Yemen as a whole.

System context

From rule to result, every link needs evidence.

A reform, new payment rail (payment system) or programme can matter for inclusion through a chain that runs from a rule or investment to implementation, operation, reachable access, actual use, service quality and protection, and finally outcome. The evidence stops at the furthest stage it actually supports; it does not cross an unmeasured link. Across the wider picture, people and capability, firms and income, providers, payment rails, remittance and capital flows, regulation and consumer protection, and enabling conditions and constraints are related but not interchangeable. Those links show context, dependency or plausible mechanisms where evidence supports them; they are not causal arrows or a composite score.

When was it measured or observed?2024–2026
How the payment architecture is changing
Payment-reform rules, projects, decisions and institutions documented by the Central Bank of Yemen – Aden (CBY-Aden), the World Bank and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), with rules, projects, integration, institutions, operation and use kept separate

What we still do not know

The gaps the evidence cannot yet close

The evidence available here cannot yet support a reliable national map of operating financial access points, a current population inclusion rate, or a causal explanation for any measured gap. Those are visible knowledge gaps, not values to be filled in.

Related measurement priorities

Each priority below describes evidence that is still missing for one of these gaps. Listing it here does not claim that collecting that evidence would close the gap or explain it.

  • A current people-side inclusion baseline
  • Financial inclusion across population groups: measure disparities before explaining them
  • A register of active financial access points
Verify the evidence

Challenge the answer

Open the evidence record to see the definition, population covered, calculation base, period, geography, method, source, derivation, limitations and what would change it. Where credible figures disagree, compare those fields before comparing the values.

Featured Reading

Evidence periodGlobal Findex fieldwork November 2022 – January 2023 · point-of-sale (POS) counts March 2025 – June 2026 · institutional records June–August 2026
The system is changing. What has reached people?

Yemen’s rules, institutions and payment infrastructure have moved faster than its representative evidence about people. The gap between the two is not an answer to guess; it is the next thing to measure.
